text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The House of Representatives of the Moslem-Croat federation is due to convene to resolve the ownership of apartments used by soldiers who have only temporary tenancy rights.

- The Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian presidential envoy Franjo Greguric discuss preparations for an upcoming meeting between the Izetbegovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
- The ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) will not support any kind of division of Bosnia and that is the party's firm attitude, says SDA secretary general Mirsad Ceman.

- Representatives from Bosnia's political parties warn the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) that upcoming local elections in disputed town of Brcko will provide an opportunity for Serb manipulation.
- The United States will continue to lend strong support to an integral Bosnia with its two multi-ethnic entities, says U.S. envoy to former Yugoslavia, Richard Gelbard.

- Some 458,000 Bosnians were employed in February, with 338,000 in the federation and the rest in the Serb entity, according to government statistics. Twice that number were employed before the war started in 1992.
- The director of Bosnia's railway network, Nedzad Brankovic, appeals to officials from both entities and foreign experts to forge an agreement which will enable the railway to start running.
- Former U.S. presidential candidate Bob Dole accepts invitation from Bosnia's co-prime minister, Haris Silajdzic, to visit Bosnia, state news agency says.

- Croatia wants Bosnia to be a strong country not only for the sake of cooperation but for Croats living in Bosnia, says Franjo Greguric, Croatian presidential envoy. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387 71 663 864
